section_sequence.what_it_does: Logo plus five white links on a grainy electric-blue strip that ends in a scalloped (wavy) edge.
Centered serif headline, a one-line dek and an oversized dark app-icon button over a soft pastel gradient, above a cropped browser mock of a chat answer.
Scalloped transition back to blue; a large pale quote ('Arc is the Chrome replacement I've been waiting for.'), a press logo, Mac/Windows download buttons, and a tilted browser screenshot.
A thin cream strip with a single line of press quotes and outlet names running horizontally.
Centered blue headline and a small dek over a large browser mock showing an image gallery.
The same centered-headline-over-screenshot pattern, with a blue event-poster page inside the mock.
The same pattern; a split-view mock with a floating theme-picker panel overlapping its corner.
Headline, a short paragraph and a text link only, with no image, as a quiet beat.
Four short blue user quotes in a row, each with a small outlined handle tag, under three small doodle icons, on cream.
Blue band with 'Enter your new home on the internet' and a white download pill, then two small link columns and a script-style company signature.

motion.observed: The chat answer builds up in stages: 'Thinking…' → 'Read 6 tabs' with source chips → 'Thought for 5 seconds' plus the answer text.
Once scrolled, the promo collapses into a sticky bar under the nav holding the headline and a small 'Try Dia' pill; it stays pinned through the footer on both desktop and mobile.
The quote is faint at first and brightens as it scrolls in. The screenshot below goes from a purple-tinted overlay to full colour.
The quote line sits at a different horizontal offset in successive frames (inferred: a marquee).
The tint of both mocks cycles between frames while their layout holds still: Spaces goes purple → pink → orange, and Setup goes green → blue → yellow (4 videos on the page, so likely video).

reduced_motion: The hero shows the finished chat answer, the same as the settled intro state; otherwise no visible difference. running_animations is 5 in both runs, so reduced motion does not stop the CSS animations.
mobile: The nav becomes a centered logo plus a hamburger on the blue band, and the Dia headline wraps to two lines. The Dia promo collapses into the same sticky headline + 'Try Dia' bar once scrolled. The press hero swaps the Mac/Windows buttons for an App Store button and a 'get a download link' line. Each feature keeps the centered-headline-over-mock pattern at small size. No testimonial row appears; the page ends in an email-capture form with a red 'Get Download Link' button.
adaptable_ideas: Use a scalloped or wavy band edge as the section divider signature, so colour blocks read as playful rather than boxed.
Repeat one feature rhythm: a centered 2-line headline, a 1-line dek, then one large product mock; break it with a text-only beat (privacy) before the testimonials.
Collapse a hero promo into a slim sticky bar (headline + small CTA pill) after it leaves the viewport, so the offer follows the reader without a modal.
Replace a device-mismatched desktop download CTA with 'email me the link' on mobile.
capture_issues: desktop-full paints the sticky nav and Dia bar in the middle of the page (just above the testimonials), and the top nav is missing from the start.
mobile-full paints the fixed nav and Dia bar over the footer.
The tinted-to-colour change in the press screenshot may be partly a video still loading.
